newsitem.title: USA: Estee Lauder well positioned to meet 97 goals.
newsitem.headline: Estee Lauder well positioned to meet 97 goals.

text.p: Estee Lauder Cos Inc said on Tuesday it was "well positioned" to meet its objectives for fiscal year 1997.

The prestige cosmetics company also said its worldwide net sales for the second quarter were up nine percent to $941.5 million. Only Japan saw a decrease in sales, falling two percent, due to the continued strength of the U.S. dollar versus the yen.
The company said also it faced selective price reductions, competitive pricing on new items and difficult market conditions in Japan.
Estee Lauder posted earnings for the second quarter, ended December 31, of $0.54 per share, compared to pro forma $0.45 a year earlier. The First Call estimate was $0.52 per share.
The First Call estimate for the full fiscal year is $1.40 per share.

The company said second-quarter sales of make-up grew 17 percent from a year ago. Skin care product sales grew nine percent due to the successful launch of Estee Lauder's Fruition Extra and Nutritious Bio-Moisture Complex, and Clinique's Moisture On Line, as well as existing product growth.
Fragrance sales increased three percent, primarily due to the launch of "tommy girl" in the U.S. and the continued global success of Estee Lauder "pleasures" and "tommy," the company said.

Estee Lauder said its sales grew 11 percent in the Americas region in the quarter, to $525.4 million. In Europe, the Middle East and Africa, sales were $266.7 million, a 13 percent increase from a year earlier.
On a local currency basis, Asia/Pacific net sales grew three percent, driven by strong increases in every market in the region except Japan, Estee Lauder said.
